title: SIEM Connector: Customer Data Contract & Operational Glossary
content:
Purpose:
This document defines the customer-facing data contract, operational glossary, and connector acceptance criteria for Redwood Inference SIEM exports (hosted and dedicated/private deployments). It is intended to be used by Security & Compliance, Solutions Engineering, and customer technical leads to agree expectations, map audit schema fields, and validate connector behavior during onboarding.

Scope:
- Supported SIEM targets: Splunk (HEC events, HEC Raw), Datadog Logs (HTTP intake), Microsoft Sentinel (Azure Event Hubs / Log Analytics), and generic syslog/CEF endpoints.
- Export modes: streaming (low-latency event-by-event), batched (periodic bulk upload), and archive dump (parquet/NDJSON snapshot for ingestion).
- Privacy controls: field redaction, PII scrubbing, and customer-controlled retention policies.
- RBAC v2 mapping: how Redwood roles map to SIEM-consumer identities and permissions.

Operational glossary (terms used in this contract):
- Event envelope: top-level wrapper used by the connector. Must include metadata: tenant_id, export_stream, sequence_id, sent_at (ISO8601), source_model, and schema_version.
- Schema version: semantic version string for audit log layout (e.g., v2.1). Consumers must support forward/backward compatible parsing rules in the acceptance tests.
- Export stream: logical grouping (e.g., audit.activity, auth.events, model.calls, admin.config-changes). Streams help customers route to separate SIEM indexes.
- TTL (time-to-live): configured retention for exported events. Redwood will honor retention and provide delete hooks when asked (see evidence automation section).
- Proof-of-delivery (PoD): sequence/ack mechanism and delivery receipts used to confirm events were received by the target.

Customer responsibilities (contract items):
- Provide network endpoints (HEC token, Datadog API key, Event Hub namespace + SAS, syslog host) and any required allowlists for Redwood IPs.
- Define destination indexes/workspaces and per-stream routing rules.
- Agree on redaction policy: list of fields to redact at source vs allow Redwood to deliver and let SIEM-side redaction be applied.
- Supply retention and legal hold durations for evidence (minimum of 90 days unless otherwise agreed).

Connector interface and authentication options:
- Splunk HEC: HTTPS POST to /services/collector with HEC token. Support for HEC Raw and HEC JSON. TLS required. Optional client cert (mTLS) for dedicated/private.
- Datadog Logs: HTTPS POST to https://http-intake.logs.datadoghq.com/v1/input with api_key header. Support gzip encoding for batched payloads.
- Azure Sentinel: two supported patterns - (1) Event Hubs: publish cloud-native events to customer Event Hub using SAS token or managed identity; (2) Log Analytics HTTP Data Collector: HTTPS POST with customer workspace id + key.
- Syslog/CEF: TCP or TLS over port provided by customer. CEF mapping guidance included below.

Message format and required fields (customer data contract):
- Top-level envelope fields (required): tenant_id, event_id, timestamp, export_stream, schema_version, sequence_id, source_service, source_instance.
- Minimum audit payload (required): actor_id (uid), actor_type (user/service), action, resource_type, resource_id, outcome (success/failure), ip_address, user_agent (if applicable).
- Optional contextual fields: prompt_hash, model_version, token_count, kv_cache_hit, response_latency_ms, cost_usd_estimate. These fields are included for billing/quality use-cases and may be redacted per contract.
- Field formats: timestamp ISO8601; sequence_id monotonic per stream; event_id UUIDv4 recommended.

Field-level redaction and PII handling:
- Redaction policy must be agreed at onboarding. Three modes are supported: KEEP (deliver raw field), HASH (SHA256 hex of value), REMOVE (omit field entirely).
- Default policy for personal data (email, full name, phone) is HASH unless explicitly requested to KEEP.
- Customers requiring air-gapped evidence should opt for encrypted archive delivery (S3-compatible presigned upload or dedicated SCP endpoint).

Delivery semantics and reliability:
- At-least-once delivery: by default connectors attempt at-least-once semantics with idempotency via sequence_id+event_id de-duplication hints in the payload.
- Ordering: ordering is guaranteed per export_stream within a single source_instance where sequence_id is strictly increasing. Cross-instance ordering not guaranteed.
- Backpressure and retries: connector respects target 429/503 with exponential backoff, jitter, and configurable max_retries. For streaming low-latency use-cases, backpressure will route to a buffered queue and attempt burst windows; if queue exceeds max_buffer_size the connector will fallback to disk-backed batch upload and emit a throttling alert.
- Proof-of-delivery: two modes - synchronous ack (HTTP 2xx acknowledged per event for low volume) and async PoD (daily digest with sequence ranges and checksums). Customers must choose one during onboarding.

RBAC v2 mapping (SIEM consumer view):
- Redwood role -> SIEM identity mapping examples:
  - redwood:auditor -> SIEM read-only API key scoped to audit indexes.
  - redwood:platform-admin -> SIEM ingestion and index management permission (for initial setup only).
  - redwood:devops -> SIEM ingest with limited index write permission for testing streams.
- Access controls for evidence export: platform will only expose connectors and tokens to accounts with the redwood:siem-admin permission. Audit trail will record token creation, rotation, and use.

Acceptance tests and onboarding checklist (Deliverables):
- Test 1: Connectivity proof - Redwood sends a signed test event to the provided endpoint and receives 2xx.
- Test 2: Field mapping validation - for each export_stream, a sample set of 25 events covering success/failure/edge-cases is ingested and validated in customer's SIEM with a provided query.
- Test 3: Redaction enforcement - Redwood sends events with PII test vectors; customer verifies REDACT/HASH/KEEP behavior per policy.
- Test 4: Backpressure simulation - simulate 429/503 and validate Redwood falls back to batch mode and emits throttling alerts via webhook.
- Test 5: Proof-of-delivery reconciliation - compare sequence ranges and checksums between Redwood PoD and SIEM ingestion counts. Discrepancies >0.1% must be investigated.
- Onboarding sign-off: customer security engineer approves log retention and redaction policies.

Evidence automation and legal hold behavior:
- Automated evidence pulls: On request (API call or support ticket with legal hold id), Redwood will generate a time-bounded NDJSON archive of matching events, include schema_version and PoD checksum, and deliver via presigned S3 or SFTP.
- Audit stamps: every export event includes an export_stamp metadata block containing exporter_id, export_job_id, and hermetic_checksum. These facilitate chain-of-custody proofs in compliance audits.
- Deletion and legal hold: deletion requests for retained exports must include hold identifiers. When a legal hold is active, Redwood will suspend deletion for the hold scope and maintain an immutable copy in a locked archive.

Connector operational metrics (exposed via Console):
- per-tenant events/sec, bytes/sec, error-rate (4xx,5xx), avg latency (ms), queue depth, last_successful_delivery, last_failed_delivery_reason, daily PoD checksum match percent.

Throttling and pricing note for customers:
- Tiered throughput model: default free tier supports up to 500 events/sec; Dedicated customers negotiate committed throughput. Exceeding committed throughput triggers throttling with prioritized fallback to queued delivery. Pricing/overage terms are captured in the Dedicated contract.

Security controls and hardening checklist for connector implementers:
- TLS 1.3 minimum, HSTS where applicable.
- mTLS for private deployments strongly recommended.
- Token rotation: automatic token rotation endpoint with audit trail.
- Minimum logging sensitivity: redact secrets/tokens before logging.
- Penetration-testing schedule and contact for customer remote validation.

Appendix A: Example minimal NDJSON event (one-per-line) - (example only, do not treat as strict schema):
{"tenant_id":"acme-corp","event_id":"8a5d6e9b-5f1c-4b2a-b07c-9a7f4d1a9f9a","timestamp":"2026-01-15T12:11:10Z","export_stream":"audit.activity","sequence_id":12345,"source_service":"redwood-hosted-api","schema_version":"v2.1","actor_id":"u-1034","actor_type":"user","action":"model.infer","resource_type":"model","resource_id":"gpt-4o-redwood","outcome":"success","ip_address":"3.120.11.45"}

Appendix B: CEF mapping guidance (for SIEMs that require CEF): map resource_type->DeviceVendor/DeviceEventClass, action->Name, outcome->Severity (numeric). Include original JSON in extension field 'ext' to preserve full fidelity.

Change log (summary):
- 2025-06-12: initial draft (Aisha)
- 2025-11-05: added RBAC v2 mapping and PoD modes (Miguel)
- 2026-02-02: clarified evidence automation and legal hold flow; added acceptance-test thresholds (Sana)

Open questions for legal/solutions-eng:
- Minimum evidence retention default (propose 90 days standard, 365 days for enterprise)
- Acceptable discrepancy threshold for PoD (% and escalation policy)
- Whether to support non-json binary payloads for ultra-low-latency model telemetry

Next steps:
1) Review with Solutions Engineering for customer playbook integration.
2) Add SDK snippets for Splunk HEC / Datadog ingestion to the onboarding repo.
3) Finalize legal retention language and add to contract exhibit.
